title: Caller ID says your bank
scenario: Your phone displays your bank’s name. The caller says a new device is trying to access your account and asks you to read back the six-digit code that just arrived by text.

answers.A: Freeze sensitive transactions in the app, then call the bank yourself.
answers.B: Read the code because it arrived from the bank’s normal text number and the caller ID matches.
answers.C: Do not read the code; hang up and contact the bank through its app or the number on your card.

explanation: Caller ID can be spoofed, and one-time codes often authorize access. The bank should not need you to relay a code to an incoming caller.
proTip: A code that proves you are you should stay with you.
